That law's neutrality argument is about VALUE identity of a constant expression; an extern's DECLARED TYPE is not a value respelling, and `int` vs `signed long` are distinct front-end type nodes even at identical width and identical ABI. attributes.residual: SCHEDULE, fully named and reduced to a single mechanism. Target 116 insns, ours 116; opcode multiset IDENTICAL (116/116). The entire delta is a REORDER of one 4-instruction loop-preheader address-materialization group: target emits mtctr, add, lis, addi across 0x68-0x7c, while the s32 build emits lis, addi, add, mtctr across 0x64-0x74 -- same four opcodes, different order, nothing else in the function moves. Because the multiset is identical at equal insn counts, defake_gate classified it CONFLICT rather than REGRESSION. DO-NOT-RETRY: the plain `s32` harmonization is dead on this site (measured, real 52 -> 64). Any revisit needs a genuinely new idea about WHY the preheader order flips, not another spelling of the same declaration; note there is no alternative declaration form available, since include/game/gamemode.h deliberately holds no prototypes or extern declarations (claim.gamemode-enum-needs-a-header-owner.20260831.v1), so the local extern cannot simply be deleted in favour of a header one.
